edition.title: The Ceremonies of the Roman Rite Described

passages.context: Fortescue identifies a portable holy-water stoup and sprinkler for the Asperges and blessings, says that the vessel is metal, and documents two sprinkler forms: a brush-ended form and a perforated hollow globe. The page supports those bounded identities and variants only, not a universal vessel handle, taper, foot, waterline, dimensions, or ornament.
passages.notes: Read visually in the exact remote modern-typeset witness. The previously proposed p. 17 locator belongs to the revised 1943 pagination; this first-edition witness places the paragraph on printed p. 16.

work.author: Adrian Fortescue; revised by J. B. O'Connell
work.description: An English ceremonial manual first published by Adrian Fortescue in 1917 and repeatedly revised by J. B. O'Connell. It describes the ministers, appointments, vesture, and ceremonial execution of the Roman Rite. Printed page numbers are the conventional locus system; edition-specific claims must identify the exact revision consulted.
